=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:lines 367-382 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The condition combines two refusal paths with `or`, but only the second one (tracked + no finding_id) is the new behavior. The first path (`security_metadata_unsafe`) was already present and was previously gated by `not ctx["tracking"]`.
  WHY: It does not fail — the conditional return of `["comment", "telegram"]` matches both the pre-existing test and the new assertions (`test_security_reissue_keeps_a_finding_open_or_transfers_its_marker` asserts `[op["op"] for op in unbound] == ["comment", "telegram"]` for the unbound path). The marker is then added only when `security_finding_id` is truthy (`if security_issue and ctx.get("security_finding_id")`), and integration-branch / depends-on lines remain gated by `not ctx["tracking"]`, so they do not leak into tracked fix-up bodies.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 16955-16960 | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: A non-regex failure from `grep` (for example a missing or unreadable `${req_body}`) would still make the surrounding `if` test pass when grep exits 2 by accident of `set -e` semantics, but more importantly the check rejects legitimate-looking markers with unusual characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.
  WHY: A security successor for a finding whose ID happens to contain a character outside the allowed set would be created without the `ai:security` label, breaking the "successor bound to the finding" contract from the recommendation. The defense-in-depth in `unblock_actions.py` still keeps the original finding open, but the split loses its binding.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 16955-16969 | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The new label is added as an implicit side effect of marker presence, with no explicit verification that GitHub actually applied the label.
  WHY: If `gh issue create` accepts the call but silently drops the `ai:security` label (e.g. label rename race, repo setting), the security successor is filed without the binding label. The successor is then managed by the normal fix-up flow but the security scan / unblock scan would not detect it as a security successor (it lacks `ai:security`). The defense-in-depth in `unblock_actions.py` keeps the original open, but the link between them is lost.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
